subject: Temporary uptime recalibration & proportional remedy allocation — North America pilot
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stargaze.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Alexei Romanov <alexei@stargaze.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime recalibration for June pilot

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick follow-up: we’re about to push a high-concurrency batched workload into production for the North America pilot next week. Based on the load profile the engineering team shared, we expect a transient bump in reconciliation and model warmup that could depress our measured availability for June.

To proceed we’d like Redwood to consider a temporary recalibration to the uptime floor for June only — from 99.95% to 99.90% — while we complete optimizer tuning and KV cache warmups. In return we propose a proportional remedy allocation: cap monthly credits for June at 10% of the standard payout and nominate a remediation playbook (we’ve attached a performance snapshot and a deployment diagram).

Goal: keep the integration moving without renegotiating long-term SLOs. Please let me know what information you need (telemetry, trace samples, timeline). We can provide a 72-hour notice before the rollout.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure
Stargaze AI

Attachments: stargaze_perf_snapshot_Jun2025.csv, deployment-diagram.png

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stargaze.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime recalibration for June pilot

Samir —

Appreciate the heads-up and the detailed snapshot. We’re open to a timebound approach for pilots but want to protect both sides operationally. High level proposal from Redwood:

- Temporary uptime floor for NA region for June: 99.90% (as requested).
- Remedy structure: limit total monthly credit for June to 10% of the normal availability payout. Any single incident credit still follows our incident verification workflow.
- Latency carveout: if P95 latency increases > 2x baseline then customer may elect a latency-based credit instead of availability credit (we’ll need the baseline traces).
- Governance: Stargaze provides 72-hour rollout notice and post-rollout telemetry (prefix hit rates, P95/P99, error rates). Redwood reserves right to exclude maintenance windows already scheduled.

Ben, Laura — tagging you for ops/contract input. Specific asks for Stargaze: can you share the baseline P95/P99 traces and the KV cache hit-rate for the previous 30 days? Also confirm whether APAC rollout is coming in June (that would be a separate carve-out).

If the above looks acceptable we can draft a one-page amendment and a DocuSign addendum that limits the change to June and lists the telemetry required for validation.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: internal SLA amendment template (to be drafted)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir.patel@stargaze.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime recalibration for June pilot

Looping in my thoughts from an SRE/ops perspective. Quick notes:

- I prefer avoiding blanket uptime floor changes where possible; availability masks a lot of failure modes. Suggest we keep the availability SLA intact but allow a latency SLO exception tied to specific endpoints used by the batched workload (e.g., /generate-batch).
- Proposed alternative: maintain 99.95% availability; permit P95 latency target to be relaxed from 250ms -> 500ms for the named endpoints for June. Credits would be calculated on latency SLO misses (so credits are proportional to latency regression rather than availability).
- Verification: require request-level IDs and span traces for a 48-hour window post-rollout. This gives us better signal and avoids broad credit exposure.

If Stargaze strongly prefers the availability-floor tweak we can accept Vivek’s proposed 10% cap but we should add a clause preventing retroactive claims for incidents predating the 72-hour rollout notice.

–Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@stargaze.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Alexei Romanov <alexei@stargaze.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 07:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime recalibration for June pilot

Vivek, Ben —

Thanks for the quick turn. We discussed Ben’s latency-focused option internally and like that better: more surgical and avoids reopening the availability metric long-term. We agree to the following compromise:

- Keep standard availability at 99.95% for all regions.
- Apply a latency SLO exception for P95 on /generate-batch and /ingest-batch endpoints for the NA pilot during June: target relaxed from 250ms -> 500ms.
- Credits: latency-based credits will be capped at 10% of the normal monthly availability payout for June.
- Verification: we will provide request IDs and 48-hour span traces; will also share KV cache hit-rate daily during the pilot.
- APAC: we are pausing the APAC rollout for now — no carve-out needed.

Please confirm and we’ll sign the one-page amendment.

Samir

On Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 07:10 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — good catch. Samir, that path sounds workable. I’ll get legal to prepare a short amendment with: scope (NA pilot only), exact endpoints, duration (2025-06-08 to 2025-06-30), telemetry required, and the 10% cap. Sending draft by EOD.
>
> Vivek
